UC Davis Aggies are the athletic teams of the University of California, Davis, featuring a white mustang as their emblem, and their mascot image can be traced back to the 1920s. The university announced on December 10, 2024, that it had accepted an invitation to join the Mountain West Conference beginning July 1, 2026, while football will remain in the Big Sky Conference. The men's basketball team won the 1998 NCAA Division II National Championship, along with the 2015 and 2018 Big West Conference regular-season championships and the 2017 conference tournament championship.
2
Team history
The conference affiliations of the UC Davis Aggies men's basketball team were, in order, the Far West Conference (1925–1982), the Northern California Athletic Conference (1982–1998), the California Collegiate Athletic Association (1998–2004), Division I Independent (2004–2007), and the
Big West Conference
(2007–present); the 2025–26 season is the team's 19th season competing in the Big West.
5
On December 10, 2024, UC Davis accepted a formal invitation from the Mountain West Conference and will join the conference on July 1, 2026. Beginning with the 2026–27 season, UC Davis will compete in all Mountain West-sponsored sports, while football will remain in the Big Sky Conference in the FCS; men's and women's water polo and beach volleyball will seek to remain in the Big West as affiliate members and explore other options if necessary; membership agreements for equestrian, field hockey, and lacrosse will remain unchanged.
2
Roster

The returning core of the UC Davis Aggies men's basketball team includes Brayden Fagbemi, Connor Sevilla, Isaiah Chappell, Omer Suljanovic, Jalen Stokes, Chase Rawlins, and Ylan Esso-Essis. The six returning players who saw game action combined for 1,244 points, nearly half of the team's total scoring. The seven returning players helped the team post a 19-14 record and a 12-4 home record at University Credit Union Center. Head coach Jim Les said that this returning group is the foundation of the team, bringing leadership, experience, and resilience.
1
In his junior season, Connor Sevilla averaged 13.3 points and 31.2 minutes per game and earned All-Big West honorable mention. He led the Big West with a 90.3% free-throw percentage, ranked 12th nationally, made a team-high 67 three-pointers with a 39.9% three-point percentage, and twice went 11-for-11 from the free-throw line in a single game. Against North Dakota State, Sevilla scored a career-high 26 points, shooting 8-for-10 from the field and making 6 three-pointers; in the final moments of the first round of the Big West Tournament, he made 8 consecutive free throws to help the team defeat UC Santa Barbara 79-73; he also earned CSC Academic All-District for the second consecutive year and was named to the NABC Honors Court.
1

Brayden Fagbemi led the Big West with 2.0 steals per game, ranking 36th nationally; his 133 assists and 4.3 assists per game both ranked second in the conference, and despite starting only 3 games, he still led the team in assists and steals while also averaging 3.5 rebounds per game. In the final regular-season road game at UC Irvine, Fagbemi scored a season-high 16 points and recorded 5 steals, and was named to the CSC Academic All-District and NABC Honors Court. Previously at Central Arkansas, he averaged 11.4 points, 4.7 assists, 4.1 rebounds, and 1.5 steals per game; earlier at Johns Hopkins, he earned D3hoops.com Region V and Centennial Conference Rookie of the Year honors.
1
Isaiah Chappell, at 2.06 meters tall, was one of only two Aggies to play in all 33 games; as a sophomore, he started 18 games and averaged 8.5 points and 4.6 rebounds, led the team with 135 defensive rebounds, and ranked second on the team with 58 three-pointers. He scored a season-high 20 points against Seattle U, made 4 three-pointers in a single game five times, and in a road game against Nevada scored 9 points, grabbed a team-high 6 rebounds, and hit a three-pointer during a closing 9-0 run.
1

Omer Suljanovic appeared in 32 games and started 9, averaging 5.6 points and 3.0 rebounds while shooting 37.0% from three-point range in Big West games. He scored a season-high 13 points on 5-of-7 shooting against Sacramento State, grabbed a season-high 13 rebounds, and scored 10 points in the season finale against Cal State Fullerton at the Big West Tournament. Jalen Stokes appeared in 27 games and started 7, averaging 4.7 points and 2.5 rebounds while shooting 44.8% from the field; the 1.96-meter guard shot 87.8% from the free-throw line, second among Aggie regulars behind Sevilla, and shot 88.9% from the free-throw line in conference games. He scored a season-high 17 points against Pacific Union and scored 16 points on 10-of-10 free-throw shooting against UC Riverside.
1
Niko Rocak is entering his third season at UC Davis, averaging 6.8 rebounds per game, and has set program records with 58 blocks in a single season and 6 blocks in a single game. He has represented the Switzerland U20 national team and has made his debut for the senior national team; after earning a degree in chemistry, he is pursuing an MBA.
5
In terms of international background and family legacy, Nils Cooper represents the Sweden U18 national team and is the son of Hall of Famer
Michael Cooper
. Isaiah Chappell represents the New Zealand U18 national team and is the son of Mike Chappell, who won an NCAA championship with Michigan State and played in the Australian NBL. Ylan Esso-Essis is from France and developed in the Metropolitans 92 program; Jonathan Noudjihidi was born in N'Djamena, Chad. Omer Suljanovic is from Vienna, Austria, and made his senior national team debut at age 17; Abdullah Amzil is from Finland and was named Finnish U19 Player of the Year.
7
Management team

Jim Les serves as head coach of the UC Davis Aggies men's basketball team. As of February 2026, he has recorded 128 Big West wins, ranks seventh in conference history, and is one of three active Big West coaches with 100 or more conference wins. He has 226 total wins at UC Davis and surpassed Jerry Pimm on January 31, 2026.
17
Head coach Jim Les, associate head coach Kevin Nosek, and assistant coaches Kyle Vogt and Jonathan Metzger-Jones have worked together since the 2016-17 season, forming the longest-tenured coaching staff in NCAA Division I men's basketball. Assistant coach Kyle Vogt was named to the Silver Waves Media Top 100 Mid-Major Assistant Coaches and GMs and is in his 14th season with the program. Under his guidance, the UC Davis defense ranked among the national top 50 in forced turnovers in six of the past eight seasons.
6
For the 2025-26 season, the coaching staff added Fortune Solomon, Mike Kosich, and Reece Lakritz. Fortune Solomon serves as an assistant coach; he previously worked for the Long Island Nets, the NBA G League affiliate of the Brooklyn Nets, and served as an assistant coach for the South Sudan national team, helping the team qualify for the Olympics for the first time. Mike Kosich serves as an assistant coach and chief of staff; he previously worked at San Diego State and South Alabama and has experience in roster construction, scouting, and day-to-day operations. Reece Lakritz is a UC Davis student and former team manager, serving as video coordinator and assistant director of basketball operations, and has been part of the Aggie program since 2023.
9
Team home venue
University Credit Union Center is the home venue for UC Davis men's basketball, women's basketball, women's volleyball, and women's gymnastics. In July 2021, UC Davis and University Credit Union entered into a ten-year partnership, and the venue was renamed from The Pavilion to University Credit Union Center.
10

On July 20, 2021, signage installation was completed at University Credit Union Center. Full-name signage was installed at the northeast corner of the main entrance, and abbreviated “U Center” signage was installed at the southeast and southwest corners. “Pavilion District” in wayfinding signage was changed to “U Center District,” while the name Pavilion Parking Structure remained unchanged. The venue is equipped with a Daktronics video board more than 13 feet high and 46 feet wide, capable of showing replays and real-time statistics.
11
University Credit Union Center opened for the 1977–78 season, has a basketball capacity of 6,003, and is one of the largest campus basketball arenas in Northern California. In the first official basketball game on November 26, 1977, 2,600 spectators saw the University of the Pacific defeat the Aggies 78–69. On December 9, 1995, the basketball court inside the venue was named Hamilton Court in honor of former men's basketball head coach Bob Hamilton.
10
After the venue was reconfigured in 2009, the five highest-attendance games were all nationally televised UC Davis home games. The men's basketball program's all-time attendance record is 7,926, set in a game against Chico State, and cannot be reached under the current configuration; the women's basketball attendance record is 4,712.
10
The Activities and Recreation Center is connected to the University Credit Union Center. Aggie Stadium began hosting football and women's lacrosse games in 2007, with an initial seating capacity of approximately 10,000 and plans to expand to 30,000. La Rue Field is a softball field with a seating capacity of approximately 300; it underwent a major renovation before the 2018 season and was named the Sports Turf Managers Association's Softball Field of the Year in January 1999. The Schaal Aquatics Center hosted its first event in January 2004 and features an Olympic-size pool and approximately 500 permanent seats. The Aggie Field Hockey Facility held its first event on August 23, 2014.
10
Statistics

In the 2025–26 season, the UC Davis men's basketball team established its identity around efficiency and defensive pressure. That season, UC Davis went 8–0 when holding opponents below 40% shooting, 14–1 when its shooting percentage was higher than its opponent's, 15–6 when allowing 79 points or fewer, 8–1 when scoring 80 points or more, and 11–6 when leading at halftime.
3
UC Davis forced 14.94 turnovers per game, ranking 14th nationally, and had a turnover margin of +2.1, ranking 31st nationally and leading the Big West. UC Davis averaged 8.0 steals per game, second in the conference, and ranked ninth nationally in non-steal turnover rate. UC Davis averaged 15.7 assists per game, ranking 80th nationally, and ranked 28th nationally in assist rate.
3
In the 2025–26 season, UC Davis had a 12–3 home record at University Credit Union Center, went 8–3 in white uniforms, and went 3–1 in Tahoe Blue uniforms. On March 8, 2025, UC Davis men's basketball defeated UC San Diego 69–58 at LionTree Arena, with quarter scores of 14–18, 8–13, 18–16, and 29–11. In that game, UC Davis shot 50% (24–48) from the field, 37% (10–27) from three-point range, and 79% (11–14) from the free-throw line, grabbed 30 rebounds, committed 14 turnovers, led by as many as 11 points, and had an attendance of 472.
15

As of October 18, 2026, the UC Davis Aggies football team had a 5–3 record in the 2026 season, a 3–2 record in Big Sky play, and ranked fourth in the conference. The team averaged 275.0 passing yards per game (40th nationally), 166.6 rushing yards per game (44th), 32.0 points per game (tied for 29th), and 31.0 points allowed per game (85th). Individual statistical leaders included Treynor Cleeland with 1,981 passing yards and 16 touchdowns; Jordan Fisher with 847 rushing yards, 127 carries, and 10 touchdowns; and Samuel Gbatu Jr. with 830 receiving yards, 58 receptions, and 5 touchdowns.
18
Team Honors
The UC Davis Aggies men's basketball team won the 1998 NCAA Division II National Championship and has made 12 appearances in the NCAA regional tournament, winning the 2015 and 2018 Big West regular-season championships, the 2017 Big West Tournament championship, and earning berths in the 2017 NCAA Tournament and the 2015 and 2018 NIT. The UC Davis Aggies have had seven seasons with a winning percentage above .500 and multiple 20-win seasons; in 2014–15, they set a Division I program record with 25 wins, and in 2017, the team defeated NC Central in the NCAA Tournament First Four to record the first NCAA Division I tournament win in program history.
3
The team has defeated Utah State, California, Oregon State, Washington State, and Grand Canyon, including a 75–68 road win over Grand Canyon that ended the opponent's then 18-game home winning streak. At the time, Grand Canyon's home winning streak was one of the longest in the nation.

UC Davis Aggies are the athletic teams of the University of California, Davis, featuring a white mustang as their emblem, and their mascot image can be traced back to the 1920s. The university announced on December 10, 2024, that it had accepted an invitation to join the Mountain West Conference beginning July 1, 2026, while football will remain in the Big Sky Conference. The men's basketball team won the 1998 NCAA Division II National Championship, along with the 2015 and 2018 Big West Conference regular-season championships and the 2017 conference tournament championship.
2
Team history
The conference affiliations of the UC Davis Aggies men's basketball team were, in order, the Far West Conference (1925–1982), the Northern California Athletic Conference (1982–1998), the California Collegiate Athletic Association (1998–2004), Division I Independent (2004–2007), and the
Big West Conference
(2007–present); the 2025–26 season is the team's 19th season competing in the Big West.
5
On December 10, 2024, UC Davis accepted a formal invitation from the Mountain West Conference and will join the conference on July 1, 2026. Beginning with the 2026–27 season, UC Davis will compete in all Mountain West-sponsored sports, while football will remain in the Big Sky Conference in the FCS; men's and women's water polo and beach volleyball will seek to remain in the Big West as affiliate members and explore other options if necessary; membership agreements for equestrian, field hockey, and lacrosse will remain unchanged.
2
Roster
texts.1:
The returning core of the UC Davis Aggies men's basketball team includes Brayden Fagbemi, Connor Sevilla, Isaiah Chappell, Omer Suljanovic, Jalen Stokes, Chase Rawlins, and Ylan Esso-Essis. The six returning players who saw game action combined for 1,244 points, nearly half of the team's total scoring. The seven returning players helped the team post a 19-14 record and a 12-4 home record at University Credit Union Center. Head coach Jim Les said that this returning group is the foundation of the team, bringing leadership, experience, and resilience.
1
In his junior season, Connor Sevilla averaged 13.3 points and 31.2 minutes per game and earned All-Big West honorable mention. He led the Big West with a 90.3% free-throw percentage, ranked 12th nationally, made a team-high 67 three-pointers with a 39.9% three-point percentage, and twice went 11-for-11 from the free-throw line in a single game. Against North Dakota State, Sevilla scored a career-high 26 points, shooting 8-for-10 from the field and making 6 three-pointers; in the final moments of the first round of the Big West Tournament, he made 8 consecutive free throws to help the team defeat UC Santa Barbara 79-73; he also earned CSC Academic All-District for the second consecutive year and was named to the NABC Honors Court.
1
texts.2:
Brayden Fagbemi led the Big West with 2.0 steals per game, ranking 36th nationally; his 133 assists and 4.3 assists per game both ranked second in the conference, and despite starting only 3 games, he still led the team in assists and steals while also averaging 3.5 rebounds per game. In the final regular-season road game at UC Irvine, Fagbemi scored a season-high 16 points and recorded 5 steals, and was named to the CSC Academic All-District and NABC Honors Court. Previously at Central Arkansas, he averaged 11.4 points, 4.7 assists, 4.1 rebounds, and 1.5 steals per game; earlier at Johns Hopkins, he earned D3hoops.com Region V and Centennial Conference Rookie of the Year honors.
1
Isaiah Chappell, at 2.06 meters tall, was one of only two Aggies to play in all 33 games; as a sophomore, he started 18 games and averaged 8.5 points and 4.6 rebounds, led the team with 135 defensive rebounds, and ranked second on the team with 58 three-pointers. He scored a season-high 20 points against Seattle U, made 4 three-pointers in a single game five times, and in a road game against Nevada scored 9 points, grabbed a team-high 6 rebounds, and hit a three-pointer during a closing 9-0 run.

He scored a season-high 13 points on 5-of-7 shooting against Sacramento State, grabbed a season-high 13 rebounds, and scored 10 points in the season finale against Cal State Fullerton at the Big West Tournament. Michael Cooper

texts.4:
Jim Les serves as head coach of the UC Davis Aggies men's basketball team. As of February 2026, he has recorded 128 Big West wins, ranks seventh in conference history, and is one of three active Big West coaches with 100 or more conference wins. He has 226 total wins at UC Davis and surpassed Jerry Pimm on January 31, 2026.
17
Head coach Jim Les, associate head coach Kevin Nosek, and assistant coaches Kyle Vogt and Jonathan Metzger-Jones have worked together since the 2016-17 season, forming the longest-tenured coaching staff in NCAA Division I men's basketball. Assistant coach Kyle Vogt was named to the Silver Waves Media Top 100 Mid-Major Assistant Coaches and GMs and is in his 14th season with the program. Under his guidance, the UC Davis defense ranked among the national top 50 in forced turnovers in six of the past eight seasons.
6
For the 2025-26 season, the coaching staff added Fortune Solomon, Mike Kosich, and Reece Lakritz. Fortune Solomon serves as an assistant coach; he previously worked for the Long Island Nets, the NBA G League affiliate of the Brooklyn Nets, and served as an assistant coach for the South Sudan national team, helping the team qualify for the Olympics for the first time. Mike Kosich serves as an assistant coach and chief of staff; he previously worked at San Diego State and South Alabama and has experience in roster construction, scouting, and day-to-day operations. Reece Lakritz is a UC Davis student and former team manager, serving as video coordinator and assistant director of basketball operations, and has been part of the Aggie program since 2023.

Team home venue
University Credit Union Center is the home venue for UC Davis men's basketball, women's basketball, women's volleyball, and women's gymnastics. In July 2021, UC Davis and University Credit Union entered into a ten-year partnership, and the venue was renamed from The Pavilion to University Credit Union Center.

texts.5:
On July 20, 2021, signage installation was completed at University Credit Union Center. Full-name signage was installed at the northeast corner of the main entrance, and abbreviated “U Center” signage was installed at the southeast and southwest corners. “Pavilion District” in wayfinding signage was changed to “U Center District,” while the name Pavilion Parking Structure remained unchanged. The venue is equipped with a Daktronics video board more than 13 feet high and 46 feet wide, capable of showing replays and real-time statistics.
11
University Credit Union Center opened for the 1977–78 season, has a basketball capacity of 6,003, and is one of the largest campus basketball arenas in Northern California. In the first official basketball game on November 26, 1977, 2,600 spectators saw the University of the Pacific defeat the Aggies 78–69. On December 9, 1995, the basketball court inside the venue was named Hamilton Court in honor of former men's basketball head coach Bob Hamilton.
10
After the venue was reconfigured in 2009, the five highest-attendance games were all nationally televised UC Davis home games. The men's basketball program's all-time attendance record is 7,926, set in a game against Chico State, and cannot be reached under the current configuration; the women's basketball attendance record is 4,712.
10
The Activities and Recreation Center is connected to the University Credit Union Center. Aggie Stadium began hosting football and women's lacrosse games in 2007, with an initial seating capacity of approximately 10,000 and plans to expand to 30,000. La Rue Field is a softball field with a seating capacity of approximately 300; it underwent a major renovation before the 2018 season and was named the Sports Turf Managers Association's Softball Field of the Year in January 1999. The Schaal Aquatics Center hosted its first event in January 2004 and features an Olympic-size pool and approximately 500 permanent seats. The Aggie Field Hockey Facility held its first event on August 23, 2014.

texts.12:
### Men's Cross Country
[edit]
UC Davis captured its first Big West Championship in 2010 when individual conference champion Jonathan Peterson led the Aggies to their historic victory.
Records_[dead link_]
UC Davis added beach volleyball ahead of the 2019 season, joining Equestrian as the department's newest sports. The Aggies opened their historic first season with a 2–0 record and enjoyed success in their most recent campaign, posting their best start to a season (9–0) in program history.
UC Davis added field hockey ahead of the 2009 season, competing in the NorPac conference. The Aggies joined the American East in 2015 and remain in the conference heading into 2023. UC Davis has not posted a winning season since the program's inception, but finished just one game below .500 (8–9) in 2019.
texts.13:
### Women's Track and Field
[edit]
In less than half a decade, UC Davis women's track & field boasted three finalists – including two winners – for the NCAA Woman of the Year Award, which honors excellence and leadership in athletics, academics and in the community. Founded in 1991, the award stands as one of the highest honors that national governing body bestows upon an individual. Since then, UC Davis is the only Division II institution to have won the award and is one of just two schools to have three winners (Aggie lacrosse player Kelly Albin captured the honor in 2004). Hundreds of student-athletes are nominated annually, from which one winner is chosen for each state plus the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. From those 52 state-level honorees, the NCAA selects 10 finalists. The winner is then chosen at an annual televised banquet. Remarkably, the Aggies’ All-American 4x400 relay team at the 1999 NCAA Outdoor Championships featured three finalists: 2001 finalist Kameelah Elarms was the leadoff runner, 2002 winner Tanisha Silas ran the third leg and 1999 winner Jamila Demby served as the anchor.
Records_[dead link_]
UC Davis added Equestrian ahead of the 2019 season and the program instantly enjoyed success, earning their first ECAC Championship in 2023. The young team repeated their conference championship in 2024, and qualified for Nationals for the first time in program history as the #8 ranked team in the nation. It was announced on January 9, 2026, that following the 2026 season, Equestrian would be downgraded to club status, and STUNT would be elevated to varsity status in its place.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Davis_Aggies#cite_note-19)
texts.14:
### Women's Track and Field
UC Davis women's golf is led by the three-time Big West Golfer of the Year and former LPGA Tour professional Demi Runas. Runas was the first Aggie to earn her LPGA Tour card. The Aggies have posted 23 team wins as well as 22 individual victories since the program started in 2005, also making four NCAA Tournament appearances (2008, 2011, 2013, 2015) over that time.
Led by Cal Aggie Athletics Hall of Fame student-athlete Tanya Ho, UC Davis gymnastics earned their first conference title since 2015 after a brilliant 2023 campaign. Ho guided the Aggies to the MPSF title as the No. 2 championship seed with a team national qualifying score of 195.965. UC Davis broke 196 in five meets, including the 196.200 en route to the team title. The Aggies totaled three of the MPSF's top-nine all-time scores in the final month of the regular season, including the No. 2 all-time ranking of 196.750. The last eight meets of the season all went for at least 195.250.
Records_[dead link_]
UC Davis' six conference wins in 2022 were the most by any UCD team since joining the Big West. UC Davis women's soccer is yet to win a conference title at the Division I level.
texts.15:
### Women's Cross Country
[edit]
UC Davis has won three Big West Conference titles (2011, 2014, 2021) since it ascended to the Division I level in 2007.
Records_[dead link_]
In March, 2020, UC Davis women's tennis also earned an NCAA Public Recognition Award for an outstanding Academic Progress Rate (APR) by posting its 12th perfect score in program history. This is the highest total of any men's or women's team sponsored by the Big West. As a Division II team, UC Davis captured the California Collegiate Athletic Association title three times in a row from 1999 to 2002.
UC Davis became a Big 12 affiliate member for that conference's first season of women's lacrosse in 2024–25, following the 2024 collapse of its former women's lacrosse home of the Pac-12 Conference. The Aggies had only joined Pac-12 women's lacrosse in 2023–24. Led by three-time Mountain Pacific Sports Federation (MPSF) Coach of the Year (2018, 2019, 2021), Suzanne Isidor captured her first conference title in 2021, leading the Aggies to a program-best 12–4 record.
UC Davis has effectively been a partner of fellow California school San Diego State, with both teams having been in MPSF women's lacrosse until that conference dropped women's lacrosse after the 2021 season. Both played as independents for two seasons until joining Pac-12 women's lacrosse for the 2024 season. The Aggies faced five Pac-12 opponents in 2022, posting wins over Cal and Oregon while also going 1–1 against San Diego State.
UC Davis women's volleyball ascended to the Division I level ahead of the 2004 season and have not won a conference title since the reclassification. Head Coach Dan Conners will enter his 10th season in 2023.
UC Davis Softball ascended to the Division I level in 2008 and claimed their first Big West Conference title in 2010 under Head Coach Karen Yoder.
texts.16:
### Women's Cross Country
UC Davis women's water polo earned a share of the Big West Conference title in 2009, their first championship in program history at the Division I level. In 2015, the Aggie made history by winning the Big West Conference Tournament to punch their ticket to the NCAA Tournament.
texts.17:
### Women's Swimming and Diving
[edit]
UC Davis swimming and diving has captured four MPSF titles (2011, 2013, 2014, 2016) since its ascension to the Division I level. In 2016, Hilvy Cheung raced in the NCAA prelim for the 200m butterfly, making the Aggies' first appearance on the national stage.
Records_[dead link_]
UC Davis has not won a national championship at the NCAA Division I level, but previously won eight national championships at the NCAA Division II level.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UC_Davis_Aggies#cite_note-champ-20)
